newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN BUREAUCRATS RUSH FOR SEVERANCE DEALS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN BUREAUCRATS RUSH FOR SEVERANCE DEALS.

text.p: More than 58,000 South African public servants have applied for severance packages as part of a plan to streamline the service, Public Service Minister Zola Skweyiya said on Friday.
Skweyiya said by February 12, 1997, 58,731 applications had been received for voluntray severance and 39,501 applications approved.
"Of these, 24,861 persons have already left the service," he said.
Skweyiya acknowledged that capable personnel whose services were still wanted had taken advantage of the packages and that in these cases efforts were made to persuade them to stay on.
But he said the government was weeding out so-called "ghost" employees in some provinces -- dead people whose salaries are still being paid -- and those staff who were drawing more than one salary.

The programme of shaking up the service has already seen the abolition of a host of posts that were budgetted for, but not filled. "So far 18,246 posts with a financial value of 665 million rand have been abolished," Skewyiya added.
